checkB_grounding_severability.hypothesis_H0_directional: No non-read carries a CLEARANCE-DIRECTIONAL status clause (expired/ceased/lapsed/abandoned) in `why` - i.e. no verdict is even rhetorically supported by status that would favour the reader. This is the doctrinally load-bearing form: an ADVERSE status remark ('the only live-granted family here') cannot do clearance work even in principle.
checkB_grounding_severability.hypothesis_H0_strict: No non-read ('NO') carries ANY legal-status clause in its grounding field `why`.
checkB_grounding_severability.interpretation: H0_strict is the strong form: a non-read must rest ONLY on a missing claim element (All-Elements Rule). Severability is the weaker decisive form: strike every status clause and ask whether an independently sufficient element-grounded clause survives. A REFUTED H0 with CORROBORATED severability means the defect is co-mingled RATIONALE TEXT, not a load-bearing status-clearance: no verdict changes when the status clause is struck.

checkC_term_arithmetic.paris_4bis_note: Paris Convention Art. 4bis: patents granted in different countries for the same invention are INDEPENDENT. A ceased US member therefore cannot clear a live EP sibling; family status is not a scalar.
checkC_term_arithmetic.section_156_note: 35 U.S.C. 156 restricts Patent Term Extension to products subject to a regulatory review period (drug/device/food-or-color additive/veterinary). A marine anticorrosive coating is not eligible, so the upper term bracket cannot be extended.
checkC_term_arithmetic.uspto_anchor_provenance: Grant years bracketed from USPTO 'Issue Years and Patent Numbers Since 1836'. The anchor table is transcribed and flagged for human spot-verification; every conclusion is reported with its robustness margin so a +/-2 year anchor error cannot flip it.

checkD_status_non_elevation.damages_tail_note: 35 U.S.C. 286 leaves a six-year damages tail after expiry. All provably-expired rows here closed their tail before the as-of date, but the fixture's own unread_or_partial list flags 'continuations and terminal disclaimers', whose members can carry later-expiring terms - so the family-level tail is NOT provably closed and is held unresolved, not cleared.

does_not_close: No FTO, no legal advice, no clearance. Term arithmetic is applied to the fixture's own annotations; it determines no patent's actual legal status in any jurisdiction.

Grant dates are bracketed to a YEAR from the USPTO issue-year table, not read from official register data; day-level term dates are not determined. Every conclusion is reported with a robustness margin so a +/-2 year anchor error cannot flip it.

Continuations, divisionals, terminal disclaimers and foreign counterparts (which the fixture itself lists as unread) can carry later-expiring terms; the family-level 35 U.S.C. 286 damages tail is therefore held UNRESOLVED, not closed.

Sec. 154(b) PTA and any Sec. 156 PTE determinations require official register data not present in the fixture; PTA can only lengthen the bracket, and Sec. 156 is unavailable to a coating, so the reported bounds remain conservative.

finding.description: Exactly one non-read row (n=5, US5059640A) co-mingles a CLEARANCE-FAVOURABLE legal-status clause ('also EXPIRED') into `why`, the grounding field for the All-Elements-Rule verdict. A second row (n=2, EP3328938B1) carries a status remark in `why` ('The ONLY live-granted family here'), but that status is ADVERSE to the reader and therefore cannot do clearance work in either direction. Legal status cannot ground a non-read: 35 U.S.C. 41(c)(1)/37 C.F.R. 1.378 permit revival of a lapsed patent, 35 U.S.C. 286 leaves a six-year damages tail after expiry, and Paris Art. 4bis makes foreign members independent. The severability test shows the verdict does not depend on the status clause - an independently sufficient missing-element clause survives its removal - so the defect is rationale hygiene, not a leaked clearance.
finding.recommended_remediation: Move status remarks out of `why` and into `design_around`/`status`, where the other rows already keep them. This is a FIXTURE edit and is NOT performed here: the fixture is SHA-pinned into a signed Phase-0 KPI and may only be changed under the human dual-identity ceremony.

CORE RESULT - H0 'no non-read is grounded on legal status' is REFUTED at 1/6 NO rows (row(s) [5] co-mingle a clearance-favourable status clause into the grounding field `why`; the strict form H0_strict, which also counts ADVERSE status remarks, is REFUTED at 2/6), while SEVERABILITY is CORROBORATED 6/6: striking every status clause leaves an independently sufficient element-grounded clause in each case, so no verdict is load-bearing on expiry. Term arithmetic under 35 U.S.C. 154(a)(2)/154(c)(1)/41(b)/286 and EPC Art. 63(1)/PCT Art. 11(3): 11/11 status-bearing rows statutorily consistent (35 U.S.C. 156 PTE unavailable to a coating). Non-elevation holds: 5 rows are provably past nominal term yet 4 of them remain UNCLEAR rather than being converted to non-reads; not_fto true 60/60; authority envelope clean; 5/5 hostile status-to-clearance mutations caught.
non_circularity: The Rust runtime is NOT invoked. An independent CPython harness re-derives statutory term brackets directly from patent_landscape.json against 35 U.S.C. 154/41/286/156, EPC Art. 63/86/122, PCT Art. 11/21/24/48, Paris Art. 4bis and the USPTO issue-year table - not against module output. The fixture SHA-256 is checked against the KPI-pinned value. The as-of date is a pinned constant, not wall-clock.
purpose: Close the TEMPORAL gap left open by the module's three prior signed audits (structural integrity, All-Elements-Rule doctrine, CPC/IPC classification): independently re-derive, from published patent-term statutes and treaties, whether the pinned landscape ever lets legal status (expiry, cease, lapse) do clearance work it is legally incapable of doing, and whether its expiry annotations survive statutory term arithmetic.
